title: PEDBench: Can Speech Models Detect Phonetic Errors?
abstract: arXiv:2610.20830v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Phonetic error detection (PED) aims to identify phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions and is essential for educational and clinical speech assessment and intervention. Despite recent advances in speech models for phoneme recognition, their ability to reliably detect fine-grained phonetic errors remains unclear because of a lack of high-quality evaluation data. To address this gap, we introduce PEDBench, the first PED benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech. It comprises real-world recordings of spoken errors made by children (N=334), scripted error productions by human actors (N=1,188), and synthetic error productions generated using phone-conditioned text-to-speech (N=1,083). All phonetic annotations were transcribed and verified by two phonetically trained annotators. translated_title: PEDBench：语音模型能够检测语音错误吗？
translated_abstract: 语音错误检测（PED）旨在识别音素级的替换、删除和插入错误，对于教育和临床领域的语音评估与干预至关重要。尽管语音模型在音素识别方面取得了最新进展，但由于缺乏高质量的评估数据，它们能否可靠地检测细粒度的语音错误仍不明确。为弥补这一空白，我们提出了PEDBench，这是首个覆盖从自然语音到受控语音连续谱的PED基准。该基准包含儿童真实发音错误的录音（N=334）、人类演员按脚本生成的错误发音（N=1,188），以及使用音素条件控制的文本转语音技术生成的合成错误发音（N=1,083）。所有语音标注均由两名受过语音学训练的标注员转录并核实。我们对13个最先进语音模型的评估表明，它们无法可靠地检测语音错误，即使在受控条件下也是如此……
tldr: 提出了首个语音错误检测基准PEDBench，涵盖从自然到受控语音的连续谱数据，评估表明现有13个最先进语音模型均无法可靠地检测音素级语音错误。
en_tdlr: We introduce PEDBench, the first phonetic error detection benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech, and show that 13 state-of-the-art speech models fail to reliably detect phoneme-level errors.
